rule: Background 7, one 4-connected 0-shape and one 5. The 5 moves straight along the ray that meets the shape and stops in front of the first 0. It then slides along the single legal sideways diagonal: forward plus one side, onto a cell that is free and 8-touches the shape. It keeps sliding while the next diagonal cell is in the grid, free and 8-touching the shape. The start cell becomes 7 and the 5 is drawn at its resting cell.
scope: A ball approaches a connected staircase along one ray, then follows a uniquely selected diagonal while in contact. Constructive vertical runs form monotone stairs, peaks or valleys; D4 orientation gives every approach direction. Guards remove unsupported wall-hugging and four-versus-eight-contact ambiguities.

authored_scope: Supported: canonical downward-fall scenes built from vertical column runs. Random shapes are rising or falling staircases, single peaks or single valleys with steps of 0, 1 or 2, sharing a base row, optionally running to the grid edge. The ball starts above the whole shape and does not 8-touch it. The scene is then transposed and/or flipped, giving all 8 dihedral orientations and therefore all approach directions and both slide handednesses. Outcomes include no slide (flat top or notch), a slide stopped by a 0 (valley or notch) and a slide stopped by losing contact (apex). Sizes are controllable in the canonical frame. Explicit columns and marker reconstruct the fixtures. Deliberately not supported: side approaches into tall shapes, shapes with overhangs or holes, multiple shapes or markers, other palettes, and outcomes that depend on unestablished readings. Those readings are a two-sided diagonal choice, 8-only contact, and stopping beside a wall whose forward cell is free and 4-adjacent to the shape.
authored_constraints: Exactly one 5 and one 4-connected 0-shape; 7 is the strict majority colour in input and output.
Canonical marker lies in a shape column at row <= (topmost shape row - 2), so its Chebyshev distance to the shape is >= 2. Only the downward ray hits the shape and the marker always moves.
On landing at most one sideways diagonal is legal; two legal sides are rejected.
Every visited cell (landing, slide and rest) is 4-adjacent to the shape.

For every visited cell, the forward cell (y+1, x) is out of the grid, is shape, or has no 4-neighbour in the shape. This rules out a ball resting or sliding beside a tall wall that it could hug downward.
Exactly two cells differ between input and output.
height, width, run bounds and marker coordinates must be plain ints (not bool); orientation flags must be bool or None; malformed column entries raise ValueError.
height and width are canonical-frame dimensions; transpose swaps the emitted grid's rows and columns.
